newsitem.title: USA: U.S. completes largest Gulf lease sale since 1985.
newsitem.headline: U.S. completes largest Gulf lease sale since 1985.

text.p: Oil and natural gas producers submitted winning bids totalling $824.1 million for rights to drill for oil and gas in 1,032 tracts in federal waters off the coast of Louisiana on Wednesday, regulators said.
The companies bid a total $1.24 billion, the largest total cash amount bid in a Gulf of Mexico lease round since 1985, officials with the U.S. Minerals Management Service said.

The high bid in the sale was $8.05 million submitted on a Mississippi Canyon tract in a joint bid by Kerr-McGee Corp and Agip Petroleum Co, said the MMS, a Department of the Interior agency regulating offshore oil and gas drilling.

Shell Offshore Inc led all bidders with 191 bids submitted, followed by Union Oil Co of California with 129, Zilkha Energy Co with 121, Chevron USA with 117 and Vastar Resources Inc with 81 bids, the MMS said.

Rounded out the top ten bidders were Conoco and Texaco Exploration and Production Inc at 77 bids each; and Louisiana Land and Exploration Co, BHP Petroleum and Statoil Exploration Inc at 67 bids each.
Bids on 587 deepwater tracts eligible for royalty relief totalled $725.1 million, and bids on 445 remaining tracts totalled 516.86 million.
